text:
jess: Hey - customer reported invoice shows ~2.6x tokens vs what their SDK estimate reported. billing id rwd-7421. Can someone take a quick look? :eyes:

sahil: I pulled the invoice, numbers look like: invoice_total_tokens=2,287,342 vs client_reported_total=890,112. Crazy gap.

amanda: Any repro or curl from the customer?

jess: Yes, they sent a curl we can run. Repro is with a few long chat sessions where we attach a session id for personalization. Customer claims our SDK and their local tokenizer both show ~138 tokens per request but metering shows ~227. Here's trimmed curl they used:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer SK_xxx" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-std","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are helpful."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize sales call"}],"session_id":"sess-1234","stream":false}'
```

jess: Customer SDK call shows: client_estimate: prompt=110 completion=28 total=138. Metering log for same request shows: meter_prompt=185 meter_completion=42 meter_total=227.

sahil: Those extra ~70 prompt tokens look like a prefill. We have a recent feature that injects a session prefill (personalization + user history) server-side but it's supposed to be counted as "prefill_tokens" and made visible. Maybe their SDK isn't fetching prefill length.

amanda: Metering-bot, any matching entries in the audit logs for sess-1234?

metering-bot: found: request_id=rid-8a3, session_id=sess-1234, prompt_tokens=185, completion_tokens=42, prefill_tokens=89, gateway_inject=personalization-v2

support-eng: So meter shows prefill_tokens=89. SDK estimate didn't include that because the SDK only estimates tokens for messages passed in the request body, not server-injected session prefill.

jess: Customer says they passed session_id explicitly and expected the SDK to include session prefill in its local estimate. They thought session prefill is client-managed. We need to clarify docs and consider exposing prefill length in SDK estimate.

sahil: Short-term: we can add a header to the API so the client can request a preflight token estimate including server prefill: `X-Redwood-Estimate-Prefill: 1`. That would return an additional field in the response like `prefill_estimate`.

amanda: Is there an existing quick workaround for the customer? E.g., a flag to disable server prefill for their workspace?

jess: Yes - provisioning can opt the workspace out of server-side prefill injection. I asked ops to hold off until we confirm with the customer.

asupport: ops asked for the exact tenant id and approximate window to redact PII.

jess: For debugging I ran the curl locally with debug headers to show metering traces:

```
> Request: session_id=sess-1234
> X-Redwood-Debug: metering
> Response headers:
>   x-rw-meter-prompt: 185
>   x-rw-meter-prefill: 89
>   x-rw-meter-completion: 42
```

jess: So the gateway adds the prefill and metering counts it, but client estimator doesn't see it.

sahil: Longer term: two options - expose prefill tokens via the SDK estimator or change metering to show breakdown in the billing UI more prominently (prefill vs request). Both good.

amanda: William on billing roadmap — do we have bandwidth this quarter to add prefill breakdown UI?

support-eng: Quick fix for customer: opt-out workspace prefill (temp), run through month-end reconciliation, then reopen for SDKs/docs work.

jess: Customer update posted: "Thanks — disabling session prefill corrected our estimates; we'll work with you on enabling an exposed prefill estimate in SDK." :thumbsup:

sahil: Filed follow-up RFC: rfc/2026-03-prefill-estimate (internal). Will link once created.

amanda: Adding doc note: "Server-side session prefill can add tokens not visible to client-side estimators — use `X-Redwood-Estimate-Prefill` or opt-out for accurate local estimates."

jess: Closing loop, marking as support:resolved after ops opt-out and customer confirmation.

support-eng: Marking thread: resolved. :white_check_mark:
